goal: The scheduler treats a prerequisite that is absent from the active work-source listing but has a DONE lifecycle in the store as satisfied: its dependents are selected and dispatched normally, and no dangling-prerequisite witness or prerequisite-missing human-review entry is recorded for that edge.

graders.name: discrimination-screen
assertions: test_cross_phase_prereqs.py contains a case where the unlisted prerequisite id has only a non-DONE lifecycle in the store (e.g. failed) and asserts the dependent stays ineligible and the dangling-prerequisite path still applies to it

test_cross_phase_prereqs.py asserts both facets for the store-DONE case: the dependent becomes eligible/dispatched AND the claim store records no dangling-prerequisite witness and no prerequisite-missing human-review entry for that edge
docs/orchestration.md's ready-set eligibility and missing-prerequisite descriptions now state that a prerequisite absent from the listing is satisfied by a DONE lifecycle in the store

relevant: packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_workflow.py -- select_next_task's prerequisite predicate (~lines 351-378) and its _cmd_next caller (~line 898); _has_done_lifecycle is already imported at line 65
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_work_graph.py -- ready_set's prerequisite membership check (~lines 401-405); GraphValidationIssue recording (~lines 250-256)

packages/flywheel-orchestrator/src/flywheel_orchestrator/_orchestrate.py -- one scheduling pass: rows/states built (~lines 2373, 2429), WorkGraph.build + redrive_missing_prerequisites (~lines 2382-2403), ready_set calls (~line 2705) and the post-claim readiness recheck (~lines 2758-2766)
packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/test_redriver_prereq.py -- keep green unmodified; also the fixture pattern to mirror for orchestrate-loop integration tests
docs/orchestration.md -- update the ready-set gate (numbered item 3) and the missing-prerequisite paragraph to the store-lifecycle semantics
references: packages/flywheel-core/src/flywheel_core/workflow.py -- _has_done_lifecycle (~line 118) is the authoritative store-DONE predicate; task_state already classifies a LISTED task DONE through it, so this change only extends the same authority to unlisted prerequisite ids
docs/data-taxonomy.md -- the store is authoritative state; the source listing is an input surface, not the record of completion
select_next_task's exclude_ids parameter -- precedent for a caller-supplied set that adjusts eligibility while defaulting to today's behavior
constraints: A prerequisite is satisfied only by a DONE lifecycle (Status.DONE); failed, interrupted, running, or any other status never satisfies

Every scheduler consumer resolves satisfaction identically in this same change: select_next_task (and _cmd_next), the orchestrate main loop's ready_set eligibility including the post-claim readiness recheck, and the issues handed to redrive_missing_prerequisites (a store-DONE id must not reach the re-driver as dangling)
The spec-00069 bounded re-driver contract is unchanged for an id with no DONE lifecycle: same per-pass witnesses, same bound, exactly one prerequisite-missing queue entry
Consult the store only for prerequisite ids not already satisfied by the listed rows; do not add a per-listed-task store read to the scheduling pass
_work_graph.py stays store-agnostic per its module docstring -- store reads happen in the caller and enter the graph layer as data
select_next_task is exported public API: new parameters must default to byte-identical current behavior
Commit the change with a clear message before reporting done
non_goals: Do not modify files under packages/flywheel-orchestrator/tests/ except to ADD the new test_cross_phase_prereqs.py; do not weaken or delete existing assertions
No changes to the status/rollup read projection (_rollup.py) -- a follow-up task owns that surface
No changes to archival behavior (archive_completed_phases), the human-review queue schema, or its reason vocabulary
edge_cases: An unlisted prerequisite id with only a FAILED lifecycle must NOT satisfy -- an implementation that checks 'any lifecycle exists' instead of 'a DONE lifecycle exists' must fail the new tests

A dependent already routed to the human-review queue with prerequisite-missing before this fix must self-heal: nothing reads the queue for scheduling exclusion, so the next pass must select it once resolution honors the store -- cover this case

The post-claim readiness recheck re-runs ready_set after refreshing only the picked task's state; if store-satisfaction is not visible on that path the freshly-claimed dependent is released as not-ready and never runs
A prerequisite both listed and store-DONE is already classified DONE by task_state -- scheduling for fully-listed graphs must be byte-identical to today
context.notes: Regression context: the 2026-07-08 overnight run stranded three dependents after their prerequisite's phase archived (proposal P2, .flywheel/proposals/overnight-2026-07-08.md); archiving moves task JSONs out of .flywheel/tasks/active/, so DirectoryWorkSource stops listing them while their DONE lifecycles remain in the store. The operator workaround was copying prerequisite JSONs back from archive/ -- this task makes that unnecessary. _orchestrate.py and _claims.py are very large: navigate them with the serena symbol tools, not whole-file reads.
